title: Rule 90 squared

outer_product_check.claim: A_t(y, x) == r_t(y) * r_t(x), r_t = Rule 90 row from one cell

why_it_works: With A_t = a(y) a(x), the diagonal-neighbour sum factorises as (a(y-1) + a(y+1)) (a(x-1) + a(x+1)); it equals exactly 1 iff both factors equal 1, i.e. iff Rule 90 turns on both coordinates.
view: whole 512^2 torus; each pixel block is a 2 x 2 block of cells (max for frames, sum for the exposure), {sc} px per block; inferno
caveats: T = 1 discrete limit, as in G019; not a regime where Lenia's gliders live.

runs.initial_state: one cell set to 1 at the centre of a zero 512^2 torus
runs.rule_note: mu is set to the normalised kernel weight of ONE diagonal neighbour (k[1,1]); sigma 0.004 poly growth makes G = -1 exactly for every other neighbour sum

render.colormap: matplotlib inferno, A in [0,1] mapped linearly, nearest-neighbour

reproduce: git checkout <this commit> && .venv/bin/python research/experiments/VIS-talk/film.py G020   # verify only: film.py verify G020
